summary: No material directional change versus 02:07 EST. Thursday matched Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54%, NVDA -4.34%, AMD +5.86%, AVGO +5.54% remain the latest confirmed US cash-session observations. Investing.com November 13 01:14 ET update describes US futures turning lower, but no synchronized QQQ/SOX session observations. Friday Asian-session WSJ reports 2Y Treasury 4.861% and 10Y 5.128% (26.7bp curve), with 87%/13% odds of 25bp/50bp December Fed hikes; quote timing is publication-context rather than a matched live feed. Reuters syndicated Friday oil coverage reports Brent $95.45 and WTI $88.39, asynchronous. Open Watch is now 162 curated events, up from 160, with AMD/PsiQuantum and Cerebras/Microsoft items; neither demonstrates a material near-term Nasdaq price response. October PPI is still pending at 08:30 ET. Friday matched breadth, QQQ/SOX, VXN/VIX and CME FedWatch unavailable.
bullish: Nasdaq closed -0.39% after opening -1.47%, showing substantial absorption of the initial Nvidia shock.
AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% at Thursday's close indicate selective chip rotation rather than uniform sector capitulation.
Foxconn and Siemens data-center demand signals remain supportive of longer-run AI infrastructure spending; no attributable index response is established.

Applied Materials fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS $4.16 versus $4.06 expected and revenue $10.41B versus $10.3B; next-quarter guidance above estimates. Cisco reported adjusted EPS $1.40 versus $1.33 expected, revenue $18.5B versus $18.1B and raised outlook; positive AI networking demand evidence, not proof of Friday market response.
Friday Reuters oil report indicates Brent and WTI declined versus the previous reported session; if sustained, this could relieve inflation pressure, but this is not an observed US equity response.
New SMIC foundry commentary indicates persistent AI demand and supply tightness through 2027, a long-horizon demand/pricing signal rather than a confirmed immediate SOX catalyst.
Cerebras raised 2026 revenue guidance and announced Microsoft cloud deal, supporting AI-compute demand, without verified immediate QQQ/SOX impact.
A contemporaneous WSJ Asian-session report describes a tentative Asian chip-stock rebound; not confirmation of US semiconductor recovery.
bearish: Nvidia closed -4.34% following the confirmed CEO transition, and SOX finished -0.54%; leadership and semiconductor benchmark remain vulnerable.
Higher oil and long yields reported earlier remain valuation risks, but current synchronized oil/yield measurements are missing.
Reuters reports at least a 25bp December Fed hike fully priced, with a 15% chance of a 50bp move; hotter PPI could worsen duration-sensitive equity pressure.
Applied Materials was reportedly nearly flat after hours despite its beat after falling 3.6% in regular trade; a strong report alone has not confirmed sector-wide risk appetite.

Reuters November 13 Asian-session coverage describes higher US yields and Nvidia-linked weakness across Asia, consistent with persistent duration and leadership risk; no matched Friday US QQQ/SOX confirmation.
SMIC says AI chip capacity may stay constrained through 2027, which may increase costs and delivery delays even as demand remains robust.
November 13 01:14 ET Investing.com report describes US equity futures turning lower, without verified matched index/semiconductor prices.
WSJ Friday Asian-session 10Y yield of 5.128% and 2Y 4.861% reinforce elevated discount-rate risk; data are not synchronized with US stock trading.

editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq enters Friday with a bearish but not disorderly backdrop: Thursday's Nasdaq -0.39% and SOX -0.54% closes, Nvidia -4.34%, and opposing AMD +5.86% and Broadcom +5.54% indicate selective rotation amid an AI-leadership shock. Overnight reports of softer US futures and higher Treasury yields argue against declaring a rebound before matched US price confirmation. Friday's PPI remains the principal near-term catalyst.
editorial.whatChanged: Since 02:07 EST, the curated Open Watch count increased from 160 to 162, with AMD's PsiQuantum partnership and Cerebras' stronger revenue outlook/Microsoft cloud agreement among recent items. Both speak to longer-term compute investment, not confirmed near-term index price action. WSJ reports Friday Asian-session Treasury yields of 5.128% (10Y) and 4.861% (2Y), giving a correctly scaled 26.7bp spread; a separate Reuters-syndicated report quotes Brent $95.45 and WTI $88.39. These observations are not synchronized with US equities.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Higher Treasury yields and hawkish December Fed pricing remain pressure points for duration-sensitive Nasdaq valuations. Positive AI infrastructure demand evidence partly offsets Nvidia-specific uncertainty, but does not demonstrate breadth recovery. Asian chip strength and softer oil may help sentiment, yet cannot be equated with a confirmed Friday QQQ/SOX reaction. Maintain elevated downside risk pending PPI and matched cross-asset confirmation.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13: verify the 08:30 EST PPI release and measure actual surprise, rates, QQQ, SOX, NVDA, breadth and volatility after the release. Monday November 16: assess whether Friday's leadership rotation broadens or selling resumes. Tuesday November 17: incorporate import/export prices and any issuer-confirmed earnings schedule; demand multi-session confirmation rather than projecting from a single catalyst. No numeric index target is justified by current data.
editorial.bullCase: Benign PPI, declining synchronized Treasury yields, NVDA stabilization, improving SOX/QQQ relative strength and expanding breadth would challenge the bearish baseline. Robust AI infrastructure orders and chip rotation offer a foundation, but require a real market response.
editorial.bearCase: Hot PPI, higher yields, renewed Nvidia weakness, SOX underperformance, widening downside breadth and rising VXN/VIX would strengthen the bearish scenario. Elevated oil or a supply shock would add inflation risk. Avoid using unsynchronized overnight quotes as evidence of a completed US-session breakdown.
editorial.watchNext: Verify the official 08:30 EST PPI actual and consensus, then capture time-matched QQQ/Nasdaq, SOX, NVDA, VXN/VIX, breadth, 2Y/10Y yields, Brent/WTI and CME FedWatch. Monitor Open Watch's 162-event feed for a new catalyst with confirmed price impact; distinguish expectations from reactions.
